answer: Cross-Epoch Divergence Scoring. Each identity’s per-epoch behavior vector is committed to a shared lagoon of historical records, and a matching score is computed between consecutive epochs. A signal is raised when variance exceeds a threshold calibrated so honest agents drift slowly across nearby contexts. To reset a flagged identity, an attacker must sustain the costly voyage of rebuilding consistent history across many epochs, paying repeated interaction and timing costs per identity rather than a one-time fee.
